questions.question: How should the trigger reach the remote host?

options.label: SSH (Recommended)
options.description: Skill SSHes mini→note (or vice versa) and runs `python3 -m remote_control work start --go ...` over there. Reuses the existing local trigger primitive verbatim. Needs `ssh note` / `ssh mini` aliases — your ssh config currently has neither, so step 1 is adding them.

options.label: Cloud sessions API
options.description: Hit `/v1/code/sessions` directly to create a new cse_ session bound to a server published by the other host's supervisor. Produces a real desktop-visible session — but I'd need to confirm the API actually allows creating-and-bonding to a specific server (today list-sessions only reads).

options.label: LAN HTTP on supervisor
options.description: Expose a tiny HTTP trigger endpoint on each supervisor, listening on the LAN (not just loopback). Largest blast radius (a new always-on listener), and the LAN posture isn't established for the rest of the stack — would set a precedent.

questions.question: What should land on the remote host when triggered?

options.label: Headless `claude -p` run (Recommended)
options.description: Exactly what `work start --engine claude --go` already spawns: a one-shot `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits "<prompt>"` in the target repo. No desktop-visible cse_ session; output goes to a log file under LOGDIR/work-start. Matches the existing primitive — least surface area.

options.label: A new cse_ session visible in the desktop app
options.description: Land the trigger as a real resumable Claude Code session in one of the target host's `claude remote-control` server slots, so you can pick it up by hand later in the desktop app. More integrated with your normal workflow, but the creation path is unproven — may need API spelunking.

options.label: Codex (`codex exec`) instead of Claude
options.description: Use the Codex engine on the remote side. Useful if the trigger is heavy enough that you want Codex's longer runway over Claude's headless mode.

So how could we make a skill that enables the mini to trigger a note machine, a note session?
Let me look at the current remote-control setup to understand what's there before proposing.

Good context. Two key design forks before I write this — they change the skill substantially.
